d1-one-message-wide.title: One message, start to finish
d1-one-message-wide.desc: A friend's phone sends “Butler, what time…”. Inside your Mac, Ghostget passes it to five checks: turned on, one-to-one, said “butler”, you’re quiet, under 12 an hour. Textbutler sends 🤖{ 👀 } back through Ghostget right away, reads the room (your notes and the recent chat), and a local model, your key, or your subscription writes the reply. The marked reply 🤖{ … } goes back through Ghostget to the phone.

d1-one-message-narrow.title: One message, start to finish
d1-one-message-narrow.desc: A friend's phone sends “Butler, what time…”. Inside your Mac, Ghostget passes it to five checks: turned on, one-to-one, said “butler”, you’re quiet, under 12 an hour. 🤖{ 👀 } goes back through Ghostget, it reads the room (your notes and the recent chat), a local model, your key, or your subscription writes the reply, and the marked reply 🤖{ … } goes back through Ghostget to their phone.

d2-words-local-wide.title: Where your words go: a local model
d2-words-local-wide.desc: Ghostget, Textbutler and the reply writer all sit inside your Mac. With a local model, Ollama on this Mac writes the reply and nothing crosses the boundary. The reply is written on your Mac. In testing. Vercel AI Gateway, xcb and web search sit outside; web search is used only with your key.

d2-words-key-wide.title: Where your words go: your Gateway key
d2-words-key-wide.desc: With your key, Qwen 3.5 Flash writes the reply and one arrow leaves your Mac for Vercel AI Gateway. The conversation context goes to Vercel AI Gateway. Capped at $1 a day. Web search is used only with your key.

d2-words-subscription-wide.title: Where your words go: your subscription
d2-words-subscription-wide.desc: With your subscription, your Claude Code, Codex, or Devin account writes the reply and one arrow leaves your Mac through xcb. The conversation context goes to that account. The model gets no tools. Web search is used only with your key.

d3-who-does-what-wide.title: Who does what
d3-who-does-what-wide.desc: Two lanes across three setup steps. Your agent: clone + install, connect apps, textbutler doctor ✓, textbutler doctor ✓. You: after the first doctor run, Full Disk Access switch, Allow Messages, pair WhatsApp or Beeper (optional), pick what writes replies; after the second, turn on one person.

d3-who-does-what-narrow.title: Who does what
d3-who-does-what-narrow.desc: Step 1, Ask your agent: your agent does clone + install and connect apps. Step 2, Say yes to your Mac: your agent runs textbutler doctor ✓, then you do the Full Disk Access switch, Allow Messages, pair WhatsApp or Beeper (optional), and pick what writes replies. Step 3, Turn on one person: your agent runs textbutler doctor ✓, then you turn on one person.

d4-five-checks.title: Five checks before it speaks
d4-five-checks.desc: Messages pass five gates: Turned on? One-to-one? Said “butler”? You’ve been quiet 5 minutes? Under 12 this hour? Most fall away at a gate. One passes and becomes 🤖{ 👀 }, then 🤖{ … }. Most of the time, it does nothing.
